clue.text: By itself, Underworld Queen's ring

parts.note: the Latin phrase per se means by itself or intrinsically
to ring someone is to phone them

explanation.surface: A grand claim that the queen of the underworld rules all on her own.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sits in the middle of the clue; the 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth she was carried off by Hades and became queen of the dead.

clue.text: Chemical engineers dealt with a polite fellow?

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
a gent is a gentleman, a courteous man

explanation.surface: Army engineers having business with a courteous man, perhaps a spy.
explanation.definitionFit: A substance used to produce a chemical reaction in a test is called by this name.

clue.text: Deck a party provided by group of sailors

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party or celebration
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Decorating a celebration laid on by a ship's crew.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck something is to decorate it, as in decking the halls.

clue.text: Trading activity somewhere within Greater Manchester

definitions.meaning: a selling transaction, or an event of reduced prices
a town in Greater Manchester, a metropolitan county of north-west England

explanation.surface: Business going on at some place near Manchester.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a commercial transaction, and a town south-west of Manchester city centre.

clue.text: Dame ain't stirred up or excited

indicators.note: stirring up mixes things, so the letters of these two words are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A pantomime dame, agitated and worked up about something.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lively and full of feeling is described as excited or vivacious.

clue.text: Located in wood, a charming country house

indicators.note: the answer is found sitting within the run of letters of these words

explanation.surface: A delightful country house set in the woods.
explanation.definitionFit: A Russian holiday home in the countryside goes by this name.

clue.text: Relish superior church led by Salvation Army

indicators.note: being led by something means it comes first, so the Army's letters go at the front

parts.note: U means upper-class or superior in British usage
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A posh church guided by the Sally Army, perhaps with some enjoyment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relish' looks like a verb but is the noun: a tasty accompaniment.
explanation.definitionFit: A relish is a condiment or savoury accompaniment, like a ketchup.

clue.text: They sell joints, look!

definitions.meaning: meat traders sell cuts such as joints of beef
Cockney rhyming slang: ... hook = look, so 'have a ...' means have a look

explanation.surface: An exclamation drawing attention to shopkeepers who sell meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joints' could suggest carpentry or cannabis before the meat counter.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat retailers cut joints; the rhyming slang 'butcher's hook' gives a glance.

clue.text: Show off dress back to front

indicators.note: the word for dress is written from its last letter to its first

parts.note: garb is clothing or dress

explanation.surface: Someone flaunting an outfit worn the wrong way round.
explanation.definitionFit: To boast is to show off about oneself.

clue.text: Time to wander about to find treasure

parts.note: to rove is to roam or wander about

explanation.surface: Taking time to wander round in search of buried riches.
explanation.definitionFit: A trove is a store of valuable things, as in treasure trove.

clue.text: Disorder that could make one angered

indicators.note: says the letters of the next word could be made from the answer's letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A mental disturbance that might leave someone angry.
explanation.definitionFit: To disorder or throw into confusion is to unsettle something completely.

clue.text: Represent men that will show such bitterness

indicators.note: the letters are on display inside these words, in sequence

explanation.surface: Speaking for a group of men who feel aggrieved.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs from the second R of 'Represent' to the T of 'that'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sense of bitter indignation at unfair treatment is a synonym.

clue.text: City church's area slightly reduced

indicators.note: only a little is lost, so the final letter is cut

parts.note: a parish is the district served by a church

explanation.surface: A church district in a city that has shrunk a little.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of France is a major city.

clue.text: Proper place to establish a more equitable sharing?

parts.note: real means genuine or proper
a location is a place

explanation.surface: Finding the right spot to set up a fairer distribution of resources.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: redistribution need not be fairer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharing out again differently, perhaps more fairly, is a redistribution of resources.

clue.text: Old lovers, notice, turning up to grab kiss

indicators.note: the reversed word takes hold of the kiss, enclosing it
in a down clue the word for notice is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to see is to notice
X is the letter used for a kiss

explanation.surface: Former partners who, on seeing each other, steal a kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses SEE to EES, which goes around X.
explanation.definitionFit: Former partners or spouses are informally called this.

clue.text: Detesting a thing going wrong

indicators.note: something going wrong goes awry, so these letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Loathing something that is malfunctioning.
explanation.definitionFit: Detesting and loathing both describe intense dislike, so this is a synonym.

clue.text: Lucky escape from mean young lady

parts.note: near is an old-fashioned word for stingy or mean
a miss is a girl or young unmarried woman

explanation.surface: Getting away from a stingy girl by good fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow escape, where disaster was only just avoided, is the sense here.

clue.text: Procure a pint having wandered around capital

indicators.note: letters that have wandered have moved from their places, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: Getting a pint after a stroll round the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital city of Haiti is a Caribbean port.

clue.text: Nervous individual starts to dither, getting emotional

parts.note: one means a single individual

indicators.note: only the opening letter of each of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: A jittery person begins to dither and becomes emotional.
explanation.definitionFit: Being tense and anxious is described by this idiom.

clue.text: Hard money only to obtain this material

parts.note: hard cash is money in coins and notes
mere means only or just

explanation.surface: Only paying cash will get you this fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine soft wool from Kashmir goats is used as a fabric.

clue.text: Time to have English bishop involved in discussion

indicators.note: the two letters are drawn into the middle of the word for time

parts.note: a date is a point in time
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: An English bishop is given time to take part in a discussion.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal argument between opposing sides is a kind of discussion.

clue.text: Go over game at table

definitions.meaning: to span or cross, as a structure over a river does
a card game for four played at a table

explanation.surface: Reviewing a game played at the table.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to span a gap; the noun is the well-known partnership card game.

clue.text: Remarkable rasping sound is heard

indicators.note: says the word is spoken, so we write a word that sounds the same

parts.note: to grate is to make a harsh rasping noise

explanation.surface: A notable harsh noise can be heard.
explanation.definitionFit: Something outstanding or extraordinary is described this way.

clue.text: Troublesome youngster gets right inside club

indicators.note: the letter for right goes within the word for club

parts.note: a bat is a club, as used in cricket or baseball

explanation.surface: A problem child gets the right to stay in a club.
explanation.definitionFit: A badly behaved child is called this, informally.
